Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

someone pronoun

also somebody, anyone, anybody

classical

Cic. Amic. 88: sī aliquem cui narrāret habuisset

aliquis

pronoun

someone, somebody

Lewis & Short: aliquis says that someone exists, though it does not matter who; quis leaves even that open; quīdam is someone the speaker knows but does not name.

Other words

  • quis — someone, anyone (after sī, nisi, num, nē)

    pronoun · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 83: sī quis deus mihi largiātur; Cic. Amic. 88: sī quis in caelum ascendisset

  • quisquam — anyone (after a negative, and in questions that expect “no”)

    pronoun · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 21: nec vērō quemquam senem audīvī oblītum; Ter. Hec. 3.1.13 (Lewis & Short)

    “Not anyone” is nēmō, “and no one” nec quisquam (Lewis & Short).

  • ecquis — is anyone …? (in an eager question)

    pronoun · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 530: Ecquis hīc?; Plaut. Amph. 1020: heus, ecquis hīc est?

  • quīdam, quaedam, quiddam — someone, a certain person (known but not named)

    pronoun · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 177: quīdam ex advocātīs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Heus, heus. Ecquis hīc? Ego sum Chremēs.

    Hello, hello! Is anyone there? It’s me, Chremes.Ter. Eun. 530–531

  • nec vērō quemquam senem audīvī oblītum quō locō thēsaurum obruisset

    and I never heard of any old man who forgot where he had buried his treasureCic. Sen. 21

  • sī quis in caelum ascendisset nātūramque mundī et pulchritūdinem sīderum perspexisset, īnsuāvem illam admīrātiōnem eī fore; quae jūcundissima fuisset, sī aliquem cui narrāret habuisset

    if someone went up into heaven and saw the nature of the universe and the beauty of the stars, the wonder of it would give him no pleasure; it would have been the sweetest thing if he had had someone to tellCic. Amic. 88

See also something, anything, everything.
